issues.claim: §2.7's support step (6) (d) (l. 2603-2616) makes a wall stretch laid after a raised way keep its course and 'run on beneath the deck': each support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span 'standing in its band' taken into the line, 'beneath every other span ... an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit' (read by §4.5, §8.4 and §11.1), and only 'the stretch's setback, glacis and berm stop at the under-deck strip's edges, closed along them' - the band runs on. §4.8's lead (l. 7610-7612, R5-02's P8, written as VM-R4T-03's fix) says instead 'the strips S7 cuts beside that trace stop at its under-deck strip's edges, their setback, glacis and berm closed along them'; §4.1's S7 row (l. 4952) and §4.13's `wall` cell (l. 9017) 'its strips stopped at the under-deck strip'; §7.3's S7 row (l. 10883) 'its strips stopped at the under-deck strip's edges'; V06's W68 (l. 351) and §3.7.1 (l. 1463) 'its strips stopped / stopping there'; V11 §3.24.2's reader (l. 3909) 'a later wall's strips and berm stop at its edges'. A wall strip is the band's half plus the setback and glacis or berm (§2.7 `Enceinte.strips`), and the L3 band is built only inside the strips (§2.2 l. 655; §2.7 `band`); §4.8 *Gates* uses the same words for a gap ('a wall strip ends at the corridor of the way through each gate, so the band and gatehouse parts S10 builds never meet that corridor'). An S7 builder following §4.8 cuts no strip beneath the deck, so S10 builds no band there: the wall has an open gap under every raised way it meets, with no run for §4.5's casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield or §11.1's wall to read - contrary to (6) (d), T110-2 (4) ('an ordinary run beneath every other span topped at its soffit') and V06 §3.7.6 (5). Two builders build different walls.
issues.required_change: §4.8's lead: 'the strips S7 cuts beside that trace stop at its under-deck strip's edges, their setback, glacis and berm closed along them, reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`)' -> 'the strips S7 cuts beside that trace run on beneath its deck as the band's half alone - their setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip's edges and closed along them, reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`) - the band abutting each support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span in it (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'; §4.1's S7 row: 'its strips stopped at the under-deck strip' -> 'its strips' setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip, the band's half running on beneath the deck'; §4.13's raised-way row, `wall` cell: 'its strips stopped at the under-deck strip' -> 'its setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip'. Ends at their homes: determinism - §7.3's S7 row 'and its strips stopped at the under-deck strip's edges' -> 'and its setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip's edges'; V06 - W68's middle cell 'its strips stopped at the under-deck strip's edges' -> 'its setback, glacis and berm stopped at the under-deck strip's edges', and §3.7.1's 'its strips stopping there' -> 'its setback, glacis and berm stopping there'; V11 - §3.24.2's 'a later wall's strips and berm stop at its edges' -> 'a later wall's setback, glacis and berm stop at its edges'.

issues.claim: The round-5 `supports` comment (l. 2292) puts a `state` on a crossing station only once no 'wall stretch lies under it', and the new closing paragraph of (6) (l. 2617-2622) gives the one rule for such a station, inside its regeneration clause: 'a station no stretch lies under any more stands as a pier (its `ring` by (4)), its `supports` entry then carrying its own `state`'. Outside a regeneration the stretch under a crossing station is taken whole after its release (both spans `ruined` or `cleared`, (3)): V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1612-1618) dismantles it 'after `wallToWay` as after `absorbWall`, the fortification loop keeping the record while such a stretch stands'; `wallToWay` (§4.11 l. 8214-8221) spares it only 'while its deck stands', so it becomes ring road; a hand `delete` takes an ordinary run. Nothing states what the station then is - its `state` and that state's writer, its `ring` - nor what a `repairRaised` beside it does: (3) and V06 §3.19.2 (5) re-lay 'that stretch by `repairWall`', whose op targets a standing enceinte record (V06 §2.8, l. 722). A builder generalising the closing sentence raises a standing pier (no `state`) with a (4) rectangle in the ring road `wallToWay` laid on the old line - a support in a way's corridor, the result T110-2 bars; another reads the station as `dismantled` and, by T114-3's regrowth clause (l. 18557-18562: the curtain absorbed, then the aqueduct repaired, 'the stretch re-laid on its line by `repairWall`'s bend'), re-lays the stretch. Reachable on the item-114 history fixtures (a neglected ring absorbed or converted after its aqueduct toppled).
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (3), after '... it is an ordinary run (§13.2's item-114 group);': 'where that run is then taken whole - the record dropped once nothing of it stands (V06 §3.7.6 (5), after `absorbWall` or `wallToWay`), or the run removed by `wallToWay` or a hand `delete` - the station reads `dismantled` (a ruined support whose stone is gone: no `state` of its own, no pier, its `ring` kept as its place), and a `repairRaised` beside it first re-lays the stretch on its line by `repairWall`'s bend (a `drawWall` on its line, V06 §2.8) as for a `dismantled` stretch (below), or, where a way now lies on that line, raises a pier on the station by (4), slid clear of the way by (3), its key kept;'. The closing paragraph of (6): 'and a station no stretch lies under any more stands as a pier' -> 'and a station whose deck stands and on whose line no re-derived stretch lies stands as a pier'. The `supports` comment: 'never on a crossing station while a wall stretch lies under it, whose `condition` it reads' -> 'never on a crossing station while a wall stretch lies under it, whose `condition` it reads, nor once that stretch is taken whole (it then reads `dismantled`)'. Scope end: §13.2's T114-3 regrowth clause adds a run whose curtain is converted by `wallToWay` after both spans fell - the station read `dismantled`, no support in the ring road, the repair's pier clear of it. (The adjudicator may rule another outcome, provided the station's `state` has one named writer, no support stands in a way's corridor and T114-3's regrowth clause holds.)

issues.claim: §4.8 *Gates* (l. 7655-7657, R5-02's P9) now counts a raised gate as a main gate ('Main gates are where S4's and S5b's arterials cross the trace on ground part 0, or at a raised gate where the arterial's raised way was created across the standing trace'), and the same paragraph claims 'a small plaza ... in S7's L1 batch at each main gate inside the wall, taking the inner strip's setback zone around the arterial' (l. 7662-7664) - so an S7 builder claims a ground plaza under the deck at every raised gate. V01 rules the opposite (§3.17.3 (6), l. 2483-2485: 'a viaduct's or elevated road's raised gate at deck level are wall openings: no gate portal, no `gate` rank or kind factor, no gate plaza, no wall-side feature and no S9b square reads them'; l. 1423-1425 the same), and V01's gate approach reads 'the base's gate plaza (§4.8); nothing added'. The raised gate's portal is on the raised part only (§4.8 l. 7672-7673; V06 §3.7.6 (5)), so no traffic meets the ground there. Two units state two outcomes for one case (found checking R5-02's P9, an end of the rule VM-R4T-01 belongs to; no adjudication file rules it).
issues.required_change: §4.8 *Gates*: 'a small plaza is claimed in S7's L1 batch at each main gate inside the wall' -> 'a small plaza is claimed in S7's L1 batch at each main gate on ground part 0 inside the wall (a raised gate takes none: its arterial passes at deck level, its portal on the raised part only; V01 §3.17.3 (6))'.
